question.text: Per SEBI Circular SEBI/HO/IMD/DF6/CIR/P/2020/24 (Feb 6, 2020) and the operational guidelines in Box 10.5, which of the following is INCORRECT regarding the performance benchmarking of AIFs?

answer.text: Performance benchmarking is done on a half-yearly basis using data as on September 30 and March 31 of each year.
AIFs / Schemes that have completed at least ONE year from First Close shall provide the required data to benchmarking agencies.
Data for March 31 must be audited; data for September 30 may be unaudited. Benchmarks shall be reported in BOTH INR and USD.
Performance reporting and benchmarking shall be carried out on POST-TAX Net Asset Value, and AUM shall be the gross commitment including uncalled capital.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Box 10.5, performance reporting is on PRE-tax NAV, not post-tax. AUM for benchmarking is the value of total capital DRAWN DOWN under the Scheme — not gross/uncalled commitment. The other three options are accurate: half-yearly reporting; 1-year-from-First-Close threshold; March-31 audited vs September-30 unaudited; INR + USD dual reporting. The Trap: The keyed option bundles two independently wrong items (post-tax NAV + gross commitment AUM). Option C bundles multiple true items together but is correct. Note: Use the drawn-down AUM basis when populating the Benchmarking Agency data template.
